founder.intro: Revault is me, Ruud Juffermans. There is no team, no sales desk and no ticket queue: I read your intake, I assess it, I do the technical work and I sit next to you at the handover.

bio.one: I studied computer science with a minor in blockchain and cryptocurrency (business, law and IT), and worked as a cryptocurrency data specialist for the Dutch police, where I built tooling for financial and crypto investigations.
bio.two: Before that I was a data engineer at the Netherlands Aerospace Centre, and for four years I taught Python, SQL and blockchain technology online. Explaining what is and isn't possible, in plain language, is most of this job.
bio.three: Working one-on-one is a deliberate choice. Wallet material is the most sensitive thing you can hand someone. With me it passes through exactly one pair of hands, on systems I control, under an agreement we both sign.

footer.blurb: Revault is the one-person practice of Ruud Juffermans. I restore access to crypto wallets you already own but can no longer open. Non-custodial, contract-first, and you only pay when it works.
footer.noScamRecovery: I do not recover stolen funds, trace transactions or investigate scams. Blockchain transactions are irreversible — anyone promising otherwise is not being honest with you.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about crypto wallet recovery
faq.subtitle: The questions I get before people decide to reach out.

needToStart.q: What do you need from me to start?
needToStart.a: Only your story: the type of wallet, what happened and what you still have — a wallet file, a backup, part of a seed phrase or the old device. Never share seed phrases, private keys or passwords at this stage.

whoInNl.q: Who can help with a forgotten bitcoin wallet password in the Netherlands?
whoInNl.a: Revault, based in the Netherlands, recovers forgotten passwords for bitcoin wallets such as Bitcoin Core (wallet.dat), Electrum, MultiBit and Ledger and Trezor hardware wallets. Based on what you still remember — fragments, patterns, passwords from that period — I run a targeted search on systems without an internet connection. Sessions take place remotely, at my office, at your home or at the notary. You only pay on a successful recovery (standard 20% of the recovered value). Start with a free assessment via the contact form.

cost.q: How much does a recovery cost?
cost.a: I work no recovery, no fee. The standard fee is 20% of the recovered value, agreed and contracted before I start, and only due once you are back in your wallet yourself. High-value wallets get a lower custom percentage.

duration.a: It depends on the case. Simple password cases can finish within days; complex passwords or partial seed phrases can take weeks or occasionally months. You get a realistic estimate after the intake.

trust.q: How can I trust you with my wallet?
trust.a: You can recognise legitimate wallet recovery by four things I do as standard: a signed service agreement under Dutch law before any work; verification of your identity and ownership before a case is accepted; never asking for your seed phrase, private key or password by email or web form; and payment only after you are back in your wallet yourself. Anyone asking for upfront fees, offering guarantees, or promising to recover stolen crypto is describing something that cannot technically be done.

custody.q: If you find my password, don't you have access to my wallet?
custody.a: Honest answer: at the moment of recovery anyone holding the password can open the wallet, including me. That is exactly why the handover happens in a supervised session in which you open the wallet and move the funds to a new wallet yourself — set out in the agreement, with all material deleted afterwards. For password cases I work from a hash or copy of the wallet file where possible, so the original never leaves you.

chances.q: What are the chances of success?
chances.a: It depends entirely on what you still have. A forgotten password with partial memory, or a seed phrase missing a few words, is often recoverable. I assess honestly before you commit.

littleInfo.q: Can you help if I have very little information?
littleInfo.a: Sometimes. Limited information narrows the options but doesn't automatically rule recovery out. I'll ask a few questions and tell you upfront if I don't think I can help.

currencies.a: Recovery happens at the wallet level, so the currency rarely matters — Bitcoin, Ethereum and tokens, Litecoin, Dogecoin, XRP and most others. The wallet type and available material determine viability.

wrongAddress.q: Can you reverse a transaction sent to the wrong address?
wrongAddress.a: No. Blockchain transactions are irreversible. If you sent funds to an exchange on the wrong network or without a tag, that exchange's support is your route.

stolen.q: Can you recover stolen crypto or scam losses?
stolen.a: No. I don't take stolen-fund or scam cases, and I don't trace transactions. Any service claiming it can reverse a blockchain transaction is describing something that cannot be done.

lostSeed.q: My seed phrase is completely gone. Can you help?
lostSeed.a: Not if no other wallet material exists — no file, no key, no backup, no device. Nobody can recover that, including me.

inheritance.q: Do you help with inherited wallets?
inheritance.a: Yes. I work with heirs, executors, notaries and lawyers. Every inheritance case starts with verification of identity, authority and ownership before any technical work.

location.q: Do I have to come to you?
location.a: No. Sessions can be fully remote over a secured connection, at my office, at your premises or at a notary's office. Your adviser is welcome to attend.

about.metaTitle: About Ruud Juffermans — crypto wallet recovery in the Netherlands
about.metaDescription: Revault is the one-person wallet recovery practice of Ruud Juffermans: honest assessments, contract-first work, air-gapped systems and never holding client funds.
about.title: Recovery without the shady part.
about.subtitle: Crypto recovery has a reputation problem. I started Revault to be the version that a notary would be comfortable recommending.

story.one: Most people who lose access to a wallet did nothing wrong. They chose a strong password in 2014, wrote a seed phrase on paper that got damp, or inherited a laptop from a parent who never explained what was on it.
story.two: The industry that grew up around those people is split between serious engineers and outright scammers, and from the outside they look the same. I built Revault around the things that make the difference visible: a contract before work, verification before a case is accepted, air-gapped systems, and a fee that only exists when access is restored.
story.three: I say no to cases I can't win. A completely lost seed phrase, stolen funds, a transaction to the wrong address — I'll tell you that in the first conversation rather than let you hope.

honesty.title: Honest first
honesty.body: A realistic assessment before you commit, including when the answer is no.

security.title: Security by design
security.body: Isolated systems, no cloud, no secrets over email, and an NDA when you want one.

sections.body: Revault is the trade name under which Ruud Juffermans, established in the Netherlands, provides wallet recovery services. I am the sole controller of the personal data described here; no employees or third-party processors have access to your case material.
